posts.title: Teach the Model to Recover, Not Only to Refuse
posts.description: Adversarial training teaches a language model to open with a refusal, not to turn back from a harmful answer it has started. Adversarial Self-Distillation uses the model as its own teacher to train that recovery.

posts.title: AI is Competent, But is it Intelligent?
posts.description: Behaviorism, functionalism, and the symbol grounding problem, read against what machine learning actually does — and the argument that intelligence is a question of architecture, not of imitation.

posts.title: For and Against an AI becoming a Judge, or a Policy Maker
posts.description: What would justify outsourcing human judgement to an artificial intelligence? Reproducibility and availability argue for it; benchmarks, missing counterfactuals, and a legacy of biased data argue against.

posts.title: One Sample is Enough to Make Conformal Prediction Robust
posts.description: We show that augmenting each calibration point with a single adversarial example is sufficient to obtain tight, valid coverage guarantees under attack — matching expensive worst-case methods at a fraction of the cost.
